chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Erskine Tate's band at the Vendome Theatre
summary: Chicago was home to Oliver, Armstrong and Erskine Tate, whose 16-20 piece Vendome band played overtures and concerts with Bertrand, Weatherford, Hines and Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Oh, this is a good breeding ground, and this is a good town, if they'd just let it be itself, like, Chicago has always been known. Because when we take all of the greats that have come out of Chicago here, -- I got some articles I want you to look at I wrote for the Chicago Defender. And this goes back to the early '20s, and all of this. And you can see through that all the people who were centered right here (recording interrupted) Bill Robinson, END T1 S2 P2 and you would have all the horn players like Joe Oliver and -- were all here, and Louis Armstrong, Lil Armstrong and Erskine Tate. And that's an interesting man. Did you ever know Erskine Tate?
Well, I know the name. I've never met him.

Well, he was one of the great band leaders in the early '20s, and then at the Vendome Theatre he had this great band. And I guess back there -- I guess he had about 16 or 18 or 20 pieces, and they would play an overture and he had Jimmy Bertrand playing drums with him. He had Teddy Weatherford playing piano with him one time, then later he had Earl Hines playing with him, Louis Armstrong played with him. And Darnell -- everybody, Darnell Howard, all the guys, everybody. They played with him at one time here. And -- but what they would do, which is almost like what we're doing now, after they'd do this overture, then they would play -- well, they would have a whole concert. They would have a concert, say, about a half hour, and the pictures would go on. And a lot of times they would play the pictures.
The Vendome Theatre was on State Street, I think. Now, I'm trying to think whether it was in the 30 -- about 36th and State Street, on the -- yeah, right.
